extracted.intended_audience: school and university administrators, Title IX coordinators, and institutional legal counsel (recipients of federal funding)
extracted.subtask_short: responding to Title IX sexual harassment
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards for how recipients (schools, colleges, universities) must respond to allegations of Title IX sexual harassment, including required supportive measures, grievance-process obligations, documentation, and the standard of deliberate indifference adapted for administrative enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate indifference standard (administrative formulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient with actual knowledge of sexual harassment must not act in a way that is “clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances.” The Department adopts the Supreme Court's deliberate indifference formulation, tailored for administrative enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term “deliberate” does not require subjective intent, bad faith, or similar mental state. The Department will hold recipients responsible for responses that are clearly unreasonable in light of known circumstances regardless of administrators' mental state (malice, incompetence, ignorance, etc.). The standard is adapted to require certain specific actions by recipients each time they know of sexual harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt response requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.44(a) requires that a recipient's response must be prompt where the recipient has actual knowledge of sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual knowledge can arise even without a formal complaint (e.g., employees observe sexualized insults). Prompt actions could include removing harassing material and communicating that harassment is unacceptable. What is prompt may vary with factual circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment: offer supportive measures and delay sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's response must treat complainants and respondents equitably by offering supportive measures to a complainant and by following a grievance process that complies with §106.45 before imposing any disciplinary sanctions or other actions that are not supportive measures against a respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures are defined in §106.30. The rule requires offering supportive measures to complainants and prohibits punitive actions prior to a §106.45-compliant grievance process. This is an explicit revision to §106.44(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator prompt contact and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator must promptly contact the complainant to discuss availability of supportive measures, consider the complainant's wishes with respect to supportive measures, inform the complainant of availability of supportive measures with or without filing a formal complaint, and explain the process for filing a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coordinator must engage in an interactive process to determine which supportive measures may restore or preserve equal access without unreasonably burdening the other party. The duty to contact is mandatory under revised §106.44(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer supportive measures to each complainant
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must offer each complainant supportive measures as part of a non-deliberately indifferent response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing supportive measures is fulfilled as long as the offer is not clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances and the Title IX Coordinator has contacted the complainant to engage in the interactive process. If impossible/impractical (e.g., anonymous report) or if the complainant refuses offered measures and insists on punitive action, the recipient will not be deemed clearly unreasonable. If not providing measures, recipient must document why not (see §106.45(b)(10)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation when supportive measures are not provided
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient does not provide a complainant with supportive measures, the recipient must document the reasons why such a response is not clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This documentation requirement is specified in revised §106.45(b)(10)(ii) and is an affirmative obligation tied to administrative enforcement of the deliberate indifference standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation requirement for formal complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must investigate allegations in a formal complaint; in response to a formal complaint a recipient must follow a grievance process that complies with §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section §106.45(b)(1) is mandatory and was revised for clarity. If a complainant files a formal complaint, the recipient must initiate the §106.45 grievance process and investigate; the Department will evaluate compliance with §106.45 independently of whether the recipient's noncompliance was 'deliberately indifferent.'

rubrics_metrics.name: No punitive action before grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents should not be punished for allegations of sexual harassment until after a grievance process that complies with §106.45 has been followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects respondents by ensuring notice and meaningful opportunity to be heard; only supportive measures may be imposed prior to completion of the §106.45 process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies required when respondent is found responsible
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide remedies any time a respondent is found responsible for sexual harassment pursuant to §106.45(b)(1)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duty to provide remedies is mandatory and tied to findings under the §106.45 grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge triggers duty even without a report
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may have actual knowledge of sexual harassment even where no person has reported or filed a formal complaint, and such actual knowledge charges the recipient with a duty to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: school employees observe sexually harassing graffiti; the recipient must respond in a manner not clearly unreasonable, which could include removal of the graffiti and messaging to the student body. The required response depends on the factual circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator authority to sign formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator may sign a formal complaint to initiate a grievance process after considering the complainant's wishes and evaluating whether an investigation is not clearly unreasonable in light of the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signing a formal complaint triggers §106.45; this allows the recipient to initiate an investigation even if the alleged victim does not file the formal complaint, but the Coordinator must consider complainant autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: No safe harbors: compliance with §106.45 and §106.44(a) is mandatory
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department removed the proposed 'safe harbor' provisions; recipients are always required to comply fully with §106.45 in response to a formal complaint and with §106.44(a) whether or not a formal complaint is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department decided safe harbors were confusing/inconsistent with mandatory obligations. Compliance with §106.45 does not insure immunity from findings of deliberate indifference concerning other aspects of response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department will enforce §106.45 provisions independently
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will evaluate a recipient's compliance with the provisions of §106.45 without regard to whether the recipient's noncompliance was 'deliberately indifferent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient may be found to have violated specific §106.45 requirements (e.g., notice, opportunity to present witnesses/evidence) even if the recipient believes its failure was not clearly unreasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process procedural protections required
rubrics_metrics.description: The §106.45 grievance process includes procedural protections intended to improve fairness, reliability, predictability, and legitimacy (e.g., written notice of allegations, equal opportunity to present witnesses/evidence, appeal rights, rules on dismissal and consolidation, and options for informal resolution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: written notice requirement (§106.45(b)(2)); equal opportunity to present witnesses, fact and expert witnesses, and inculpatory/exculpatory evidence (§106.45(b)(5)(ii)); appealability of dismissals (§106.45(b)(8)(i)); dismissal rules (§106.45(b)(3)); consolidation (§106.45(b)(4)); informal resolution option (§106.45(b)(9)); live hearing virtual attendance option (§106.45(b)(6)(i)). The Department selected these provisions as necessary to improve grievance processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients retain discretion in non-mandatory aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients retain discretion to determine which supportive measures to offer and other procedural choices not mandated by §106.45 or §106.44(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discretionary choices include whether to offer informal resolution, whether to permit virtual attendance at hearings, and whether to take action under separate codes of conduct even when Title IX allegations are dismissed under §106.45(b)(3)(i). Discretion must still produce responses that are not clearly unreasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responses must respect complainant autonomy while ensuring fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department affirms complainant autonomy by allowing complainants to decline formal grievance participation while requiring recipients to offer supportive measures and to respect complainants' wishes to the degree possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the same time, if a complainant files a formal complaint the recipient must investigate. The balance aims to avoid chilling reporting while preserving fairness to respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department will not accept mere procedural 'box-checking'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will not allow recipients to escape liability merely by having procedures on paper that appear to comply with §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department will evaluate substantive compliance and the quality of the recipient's implementation; failures (e.g., not sending written notice, not allowing equal opportunity to present evidence) can be violations even if the recipient believes its actions were reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate indifference standard allows fact-specific flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'not clearly unreasonable' standard recognizes that appropriate responses will vary with the unique factual circumstances and allows recipients some discretion in choosing suitable measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: different responses for allegations involving positions of authority versus peer-on-peer incidents; discretion does not remove mandatory elements like offering supportive measures or following §106.45 for formal complaints.
